newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Hyundai delegation to visit Yugo's Zastava - Beta.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai delegation to visit Yugo's Zastava - Beta.

text.p: A high-level delegation of Korean car maker Hyundai is due on a three-day visit to Belgrade on Wednesday to discuss a deal with Yugoslav auto manufacturer Zastava, independent news agency Beta reported on Tuesday.
The delegation will hold talks in Belgrade with Srboljub Vasovic, president of Yugoslavia's biggest manufacturing company Zastava group.
Korean officials will also meet vice-president of industrial production Kamenko Sretenovic in Kragujevac, and director of the factory's pick-up plant Steva Vojinovic in Vojvodina, Beta said.
According to Beta, Korean experts have been inspecting the Kragujevac car manufactorers' plants over the past ten days.

The Hyundai officials are also scheduled to meet Yugoslav Finance Minister Tomica Raicevic, experts of the international auditing firm Coopers & Lybrand and a mixed bank, probably Societe Generale-Yugoslav bank, Beta said.
The Group's vice president Slobodan Radovic said last month Zastava was negotiating with two potential partners and both talks have reached the same phase but did not give more details.
Hyundai said last week it was negotiating a joint venture with Zastava.
Zastava Cars, whose production last year dropped to 10,000 vehicles compared to 200,000 in 1990, said it planned to raise production to 150,000 cars by 2001.
